title: Snake Emoji 🐍 Meaning: Calling Out a Backstabber
description: The 🐍 snake emoji calls someone a traitor or two-faced. Learn the slang, the Taylor Swift story, its Python and zodiac uses, and when it is just a reptile.
summary: The 🐍 snake emoji most often accuses someone of being a snake: a backstabber, liar or fake friend. A wave of snake comments aimed at Taylor Swift in 2016 made the meaning famous. It also represents the Python programming language, the Year of the Snake and, naturally, actual snakes.
meaning: Calling a person a snake is ancient, traceable at least to the serpent in Genesis, and the emoji makes the insult quick. Posted under someone’s photo or dropped into a group chat, 🐍 says “you can’t be trusted.” It is used for friends who share secrets, partners who cheat, coworkers who take credit and athletes who leave for a rival team. One snake is an accusation; a wall of them is a campaign.

The defining moment came in 2016, when a public dispute between Taylor Swift, Kanye West and Kim Kardashian led critics to fill Swift’s comment sections with snake emojis. Instead of ignoring it, she built her 2017 Reputation album and tour around snake imagery, turning the insult into a logo. Since then the emoji has had a double edge: it is still a slur for disloyalty, but among her fans it can be worn with pride.

Plenty of uses are neutral. Programmers use 🐍 for Python, which takes its name from Monty Python but adopted a snake logo. It marks the Year of the Snake in the lunar zodiac, most recently 2025. Harry Potter fans use it for Slytherin house, basketball fans remember Kobe Bryant’s “Black Mamba” nickname, and reptile keepers post it under photos of their pets. Occasionally it serves as a phallic joke.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Between friends it can be a joke, as in “you went to brunch without me 🐍,” or a serious verdict on someone outside the chat. The more snakes and the fewer words, the angrier the sender. If it is aimed at you by someone who is not laughing, they believe you betrayed them.

contexts.label: On Instagram and TikTok
contexts.body: Comment sections use it to side against a celebrity or influencer in a feud. Fans leave it under posts by an ex, a former bandmate or anyone accused of leaking information. It is also the standard reaction when an athlete signs with a rival, a tradition in NBA fandom going back to high-profile free-agency moves.

contexts.label: In tech
contexts.body: In developer chats, job listings and course titles, 🐍 means Python and nothing else. “Learning 🐍 this summer” is about code. Data science and machine learning communities use it constantly, and no one there reads it as an insult, even when a colleague is being difficult.

contexts.label: On holidays
contexts.body: During Lunar New Year in a snake year, the emoji appears in greetings, red-envelope messages and brand campaigns across East and Southeast Asia, where the snake is associated with wisdom and intuition rather than treachery. People born in snake years use it as a birth-sign marker.

examples.text: She told him everything I said. 🐍
examples.meaning: The sender feels betrayed by a friend who broke a confidence.

examples.text: You watched the finale without me?? 🐍🐍
examples.meaning: A mock accusation of betrayal over something small.

examples.text: Rewrote the whole script in 🐍 and it runs twice as fast
examples.meaning: Refers to the Python programming language.
A Taylor Swift fan referencing the Reputation album.

examples.text: Sorting hat put me in 🐍 and honestly, fair
examples.meaning: Identifies as a Slytherin from Harry Potter.

combos.meaning: A snake in the grass: a hidden enemy pretending to be friendly.
“I see what you’re doing”; suspicion of someone’s sneaky behavior.

confusedWith.difference: 🐉 is a long serpentine Chinese-style dragon that can look snake-like at small sizes. It stands for power, luck and fantasy, and is a different zodiac sign. It is never used to call someone a traitor.

🪱 is a pink earthworm, used for gardening, fishing bait and bookworm jokes. Calling someone a worm suggests they are pathetic rather than treacherous, and the emoji has nothing like the snake’s cultural weight.

🐀 is the other animal for disloyalty, but with a narrower meaning: a rat is an informer who tells on people. A snake deceives and betrays more broadly. In sports and gossip the two are sometimes used together.

avoid: Do not join mass snake-emoji pile-ons under someone’s posts; coordinated comments like this count as harassment.
Avoid it in workplace chat about colleagues, since it is a direct accusation of dishonesty.
Be careful using it in Lunar New Year greetings to mean anything negative; in that context it is a respected zodiac animal.
design: The emoji is a green snake, usually coiled or curved with its head raised and a forked red tongue flicking out. Apple’s has a yellowish belly and patterned scales; Google’s is a simpler cartoon. Some platforms draw it facing left in a loose S-shape. It is not a specific species and is not shown as aggressive, though the tongue gives it a slightly sinister look.

faqs.q: What does it mean when someone comments 🐍 on a post?
faqs.a: They are calling the poster, or someone in the post, fake or disloyal. It often appears during public fallouts between friends, couples or celebrities. On a Taylor Swift fan post, it may instead be a positive reference to her Reputation era.

faqs.q: Why is the snake emoji associated with Taylor Swift?
faqs.a: In 2016, people angry at her over a dispute with Kim Kardashian and Kanye West spammed her social media with snakes. She later adopted the snake as the central image of her Reputation album and stadium tour, reclaiming it.

faqs.q: What does 🐍 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: If it follows something you did, he is accusing you of going behind his back, perhaps jokingly. About another person, it warns you that he does not trust them. In a suggestive conversation it can be a crude reference to his anatomy.

In programming contexts, yes. The Python language uses two intertwined snakes as its logo, and developers use the emoji as shorthand in posts, repository descriptions and conference materials. The language’s name actually honors the comedy group Monty Python.

faqs.q: Is the snake emoji always negative?
faqs.a: No. It is neutral for reptiles, coding, Slytherin and the zodiac, and positive in cultures that link snakes with wisdom, healing or renewal. The negative “traitor” meaning dominates in English-language gossip and sports talk.
